statement: The PETG frame's first vibration mode, held at the FC posts and the strap saddle with the motors on it, is at or above 200 Hz
rationale: The printed-frame vibration complaint is a soft structural mode low enough to sit inside the flight controller's control loop: the gyro sees it, the PID loop amplifies it, the motors get hot. Betaflight's dynamic notch and gyro low-pass handle a resonance above ~200 Hz with little delay; below ~150 Hz filtering it costs control. REVISED 2026-10-17: settled by CalculiX on the printed 3D frame (quadratic tets, transversely isotropic printed PETG, the everyday filament), held at the FC posts' top faces and the strap saddle, with each motor + prop as a mass on its seat's top face; no longer by the optimiser's own 2.5D plate model. The hold is an approximation, not a bound: a free-flying body moves too, which raises the mode, but holding the saddle rigid and lumping each motor on one face both raise the computed mode above what a real flight sees. The author kept the 200 Hz limit (2026-10-17) though the PETG frame is expected to fall short of it; P2's hover settles whether that matters.

mechanism.how: CalculiX eigenfrequencies of the printed frame mesh in the everyday filament, held at the FC posts' top faces and the strap saddle, each motor + prop as a mass on its seat; checked on a finer surface and mesh (fea_converged)
